The Wix original had an "Our Services" heading and the literal placeholder "I'm a title. Click here to edit me." Phase 2 rescued it by listing the service pages derived from primaryNav, which meant it re-listed the nav and nothing else; removing the footer sitemap then left it with no inbound link. It was briefly classified redirectOnly with a 301 to /services, on the assumption an indexed path is always worth preserving. It is not: there was never any original content to preserve, and render.yaml does not govern the live service, so that redirect would have been a rule nobody ever configured. Dropped, and it 404s deliberately.

Retired from the public site on 2026-08-17. The knowledge base, the forms library and every blog article moved into the CRM, so none of this content is coming back to a public URL. STATUS IS 404, AND THAT IS THE SETTLED ANSWER, NOT AN OUTSTANDING TASK. A 410 was asked for and is not achievable here, on two counts: this is a static export, which cannot emit a status for a path it does not build, and Render's static sites only offer route types `redirect` and `rewrite`, with no status-code option. Emitting a real 410 would mean putting a proxy in front or leaving static hosting, which is infrastructure work for a marginal gain - both signals de-index, 410 merely slightly sooner. ⚠ NOT ACTUALLY REMOVED FROM THE LIVE SITE AS AT 2026-08-18. The extensionless paths 404, but every retired page and asset is still served at its explicit path - /knowledge.html, /forms.html (which names an insurer), all 12 articles, and the forms manifest and PDF. Render's static publish is additive, so a file absent from a new deploy is never deleted; clearing the build cache does not touch published output. Removing them means emptying the publish directory, i.e. recreating the service or a support ticket. See content/_retired/README.md. Do not record these as retired until each 404s to a cache-busted request WITH its extension. Do not reopen this unless the site stops being a static export for some other reason.

tombstoned.$comment: STALE FILES ON THE LIVE DISK, overwritten rather than removed (decision 2026-08-19). These 15 paths are also in `dropped` below and the intent there is unchanged: they should not exist. They do. Render's publish is additive - it writes whatever the build emits and leaves everything else alone - so the 17 Aug export of this site is still being served at these .html paths, complete and readable, with navigation pointing at /knowledge. The KB retirement has not actually taken effect for anyone holding an old link. Nothing in this repo can delete them. But the same additive publish that stranded them WILL overwrite a file the build does emit, which is the whole mechanism here.
tombstoned.$howItWorks: scripts/gen-tombstones.ts writes one small noindex page per path into out/ after `next build`. Do not put these in public/ - they are generated from this list so the list stays the single source, and so nobody edits fifteen near-identical files by hand.
tombstoned.$whenToDeleteThis: When 301s exist. A tombstone returns 200, which is worse for search than a redirect and much better than serving a retired article. If Render redirect rules are found to take precedence over an existing static file, move these to `redirectOnly`, ship the rules, and delete this block - but only after confirming the rule actually wins, because if it does not, deleting the tombstones does not restore a 404, it restores the 17 Aug page. Note the 301 would need to cover BOTH forms of each path, since both now answer.
tombstoned.$doNotAddRobotsDisallow: A Disallow for these paths would stop crawlers fetching them, which stops them seeing the noindex, which is what gets them out of the index. Leave them crawlable.

tombstoned.$extensionlessBecame200: MEASURED 2026-08-19, AFTER SHIPPING: emitting these files changed the extensionless paths too. Before the deploy /knowledge was 404 and /knowledge.html was 200; now both serve the tombstone. Render resolves an extensionless request to a .html file it published, but would not do so for a file merely stranded on the disk from an older publish - which is why the split existed at all. This was not the plan and it is accepted rather than regretted: a 404 and a noindex 200 both get a URL out of the index, and the 200 is the one that tells a human what happened and where to go instead. But it does mean `dropped.status` below is no longer true for these fifteen, and there is now NO WAY to have the .html tombstone without the extensionless 200 - do not go looking for one. The end state that fixes both is a 301.

strandedAssets.$comment: NOT PAGES. Non-HTML files stranded on the live disk by the same additive publish, found 2026-08-19 while answering whether Render can delete anything. They are overwritten by the same mechanism as `tombstoned` above, because there is no other mechanism.
strandedAssets.$whyTheseMatter: The manifest names an insurer three times in served JSON, which is precisely what scripts/verify-copy.ts exists to prevent and which its own header records as having no remaining exemption now that /forms is retired. The PDF is an insurer's client document, 1.45MB, still downloadable by anyone with the URL. Both were meant to leave the public site on 2026-08-17 and never did.
strandedAssets.$note: The PDF's path still contains an insurer name. That cannot be changed - the path is what has to be overwritten - and it is not a copy violation: verify-copy.ts scans file CONTENTS, and only for the extensions in SCANNED_EXTENSIONS, which excludes .pdf.
